title: Tag-document linking
summary: define optional ordered one-way references from canonical tags to independently managed public document placements
content_html:
Tag-document linking

Relationship Contract

A tag_registry_v5 row owns an ordered doc_url array of zero or more canonical Docs Viewer locations:

{
  "tag_id": "moss",
  "group": "subject",
  "doc_url": [
    "/analysis/?doc=d-20260624-213316-478639&subdoc=d-20260727-225608-63967a"
  ],
  "updated_at_utc": "<timestamp>"
}

tag registry row
  -> optional ordered location references
      -> independently owned documents and report placements

other tag registry rows
  -> may reference the same exact locations
  • doc_url: [] is the unlinked state. The field itself is required.
  • URL order is meaningful presentation order. The same exact URL cannot repeat within one row, but may be shared by any number of tags.
  • A URL identifies the chosen public placement, not only the source document. One document can therefore have several valid locations through different report hosts.
  • Documents contain no tag_id back-reference and may exist without a tag. Neither side has exclusive ownership of the other.
  • Deleting a tag leaves every referenced document intact. Deleting or unpublishing a document does not rewrite the Registry and may leave an unavailable URL.
  • Tag group and document group are independently canonical. Creation may seed document metadata once; later edits never compare, synchronize, repair, or trigger builds across those owners.
  • Title and content are presentation, never association identity. No title match, selected parent, displayed document, or alternate route may silently replace a stored URL.

Creation And Editing

New Tag creates one Registry row and one fresh Analysis tags source document as one transaction. The new document receives its immutable ID, tag title, submitted group metadata, public visibility, and a heading containing the tag ID. Its canonical Analysis placement is stored at doc_url[0].

Creation validates only the new candidate and its configured destination. It does not inspect existing URL arrays for uniqueness, resolution, or repair. The create-only source write is the collision boundary and will not overwrite an existing destination.

Edit Tag keeps tag_id immutable and submits the complete accepted scalar group plus ordered URL array. The UI can append one exact published Analysis location returned by the shared provider or remove one exact URL from the draft. Save commits the complete array atomically; Close discards the draft. It does not create, edit, delete, or repair a document.

The Registry schema validates supported canonical URL shape and within-row duplicates, but deliberately does not require current provider membership. This lets an association selected moments earlier survive publication churn and lets an unavailable stored URL remain visible and removable.

Resolution And Presentation

The Registry stores no document or report title. Studio resolves current presentation from compact public docs_document_locations_v1 projections built from each owning scope's published search, report, and sub-scope data. Management/source-only documents are absent.

The table and Edit Tag modal render current titles in stored order. A resolving title opens against Studio's configured public-preview origin, so local work uses the site preview server rather than the Studio server. An unresolved URL is shown as Unavailable document, retains its exact href, and may be removed.

The shared provider covers published Analysis and Library locations. The Tag Registry picker deliberately requests Analysis only, shows title-only results, and exposes no free-form URL or document-ID input. Schema support for canonical Library and Studio routes does not imply that the current Tag Registry UI can author them.

History And Boundaries

The one-off Tag Document Bootstrap Delivery created distinct Analysis documents for the 245-row cutover set and initially linked them through scalar doc_id values. The subsequent Tag Link Management Delivery migrated those references to ordered canonical URLs, retired tag-row descriptions, and delivered current inspection, append, and removal behavior. Distinct bootstrap allocations describe that migration, not an ongoing one-tag-to-one-document rule.

There is no automatic stale-link repair, bulk mutation, drag reorder, or Library/Studio picker workflow. Tag semantic-token support is also separate; if added later it must consume an explicit resolving canonical location and must not infer one from mutable text or UI context.

Docs Viewer owns document lifecycle and dense source-management controls: Manage Sub-Scope Documents. The canonical Registry schema/write boundary lives in Tag Source Data, and the current tag workflow lives in Tag Registry.
